articles.title: Everton left with only one striker after Balogun deal collapses late on deadline day
articles.summary: 25-year-old walks away from £40m deal at last moment. Beto and Ndiaye already sold by club to raise funds. Everton’s £40m move for US international Folarin Balogun collapsed late on deadline day to leave manager David Moyes with only one striker for the first half of the season.
body: Everton had agreed a £40m deal for Balogun only for issues with the striker’s medical to place the transfer in doubt after the Merseyside club had sold Beto to Fiorentina and Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City. Enquiries were made to Manchester United for Joshua Zirkzee and Aston Villa for Tammy Abraham but proposed loans for both forwards were rejected.

The structure of the deal was renegotiated late on – Monaco agreed to accept a lower payment up front and more in add-ons – and Everton submitted a deal sheet to complete the transfer in time. But the 25-year-old is said to have changed his mind over the move and walked away at the final moment. The collapse of the deal leaves Thierno Barry as Everton’s one recognised striker and completed a shambolic end to the window by the club’s hierarchy, who were already under pressure having tried to sell Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest.
points: 25-year-old walks away from £40m deal at last moment.

articles.title: Fernández completes record-equalling £125m move from Chelsea to Manchester City
articles.summary: Fernández: ‘This is a club built for success’ Chelsea’s move for Monaco’s Camara falls through. Manchester City have equalled the British transfer record with a £125m deal to sign Enzo Fernández from Chelsea, who were left raging after their attempts to replace the Argentina midfielder were dashed…
body: On a day of twists and turns, City emerged in a strong position after they bolstered their attack by signing Iliman Ndiaye from Everton for up to £65m and landed one of Enzo Maresca’s biggest targets on a five-year deal. Chelsea held out for a huge fee for Fernández and it seemed they were going to find a replacement for him as the transfer window drew to a close.

The club moved to agree a £47m fee with Monaco for Camara, who was set to sign a six-year contract with the option of an extra year. Chelsea swooped when Everton’s attempts to sign the USA striker Folarin Balogun ran into difficulties. It left Monaco needing to raise funds from elsewhere, prompting Chelsea to revive their move for Camara after having a £38.1m offer for the 22-year-old Senegal midfielder rejected earlier in the day.

articles.title: Rybakina makes winning start in race to number one
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina says she is "motivated" by the race to become world number one but is simply taking things "day by day" after getting her US Open campaign off to a winning start.
body: Playing for the first time since withdrawing midway through her Cincinnati Masters quarter-final with a heel injury last month, Rybakina showed no signs of discomfort as she eased to a dominant 6-3 6-2 win over 17-year-old wildcard Thea Frodin.

The 27-year-old second seed trails Aryna Sabalenka by just 434 points in the world rankings and will become number one for the first time by reaching the semi-finals in New York – even if Sabalenka defends her title.
Regardless of her performance, Rybakina will also secure the top ranking if none of Sabalenka, Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula lift the trophy.
"I'm definitely motivated [to become world number one]," said Rybakina, who trailed Sabalenka by more than 3,000 points in the spring before the Belarusian entered a mid-season slump.

articles.title: Sunderland pip Crystal Palace in battle of the private jets to land Malick Fofana
articles.summary: Both clubs send planes to France to acquire Lyon winger. Sunderland submit deal sheet for £31m transfer. Sunderland and Crystal Palace were involved in an extraordinary deadline-day tug of war that concluded with Malick Fofana agreeing to swap Lyon for the Stadium of Light in a club-record £31m…
body: On Tuesday morning it had seemed that the 21-year-old Belgium winger was heading for Sunderland on a five-year contract, but then Pierre Sage led an attempt to hijack the deal. Palace’s manager coached Fofana at Lyon and forged a strong bond with a player he was keen to bring to Selhurst Park. After speaking to Sage on the phone, Fofana seemed to have changed his mind and decided he wanted to reunite with his old boss in south London. Sunderland, though, refused to surrender.

That meant Lyon had a bidding war on their hands and responded by agreeing improved deals with both clubs. Agents’ fees and Fofana’s personal terms were also understood to have risen accordingly. Meanwhile, two private jets, one dispatched by Sunderland and the other by Palace, sat on the tarmac at Lyon airport.

articles.title: ‘A great feeling’: Mykhailo Mudryk seals loan move from Chelsea to Tottenham
articles.summary: Deal for Ukrainian winger has £75m purchase option. Mudryk: ‘I’m so excited to be reunited with De Zerbi’ Tottenham have thrown a Premier League lifeline to the forgotten Chelsea winger, Mykhailo Mudryk, signing him on loan just before the transfer deadline and challenging him to revive his career.
body: Mudryk became a €100m (£89m) player when Chelsea took him from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023; the deal comprised an initial €70m and €30m in add-ons. Chelsea beat Arsenal to his signature at a point when the Ukrainian was among the most in-demand players in Europe.

The move to Chelsea did not work out and Mudryk hit rock bottom when he was banned for returning an adverse reading for the banned substance, meldonium, which can increase respiratory capacity and stamina. His last competitive game for Chelsea was on 28 November 2024.

Mudryk was suspended before being given a four-year ban by the Football Association. But after an appeal to the court of arbitration for sport, he was able to resolve his case with the FA at the end of July, being cleared for an immediate return to playing. He accepted breaking anti-doping rules and agreed to a suspension that was equal to the time he had already served. The FA noted that changes have been made to the World Anti-Doping Agency’s rules on meldonium and had Mudryk’s test been conducted today then “the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported” and no adverse finding would have been recorded.

articles.title: No repeat of Wimbledon heroics as Fery exits US Open
articles.summary: Arthur Fery is unable to produce a repeat of his Wimbledon heroics as his US Open debut ends in a first-round loss to Italian 13th seed Lorenzo Musetti.
body: Arthur Fery was unable to produce a repeat of his Wimbledon heroics as his US Open debut ended in a first-round defeat by Italian 13th seed Lorenzo Musetti.

Fery, 24, was seeking to build on a sensational, breakout run to the semi-finals at his home Grand Slam this summer, an achievement which catapulted him from 114th in the rankings to inside the top 40.
But having narrowly missed out on a seeded position in New York - awarded to the top 32 players - the world number 33 was unfortunate to draw talented all-rounder Musetti in his opener.

Musetti, a quarter-finalist 12 months ago but absent from the past two majors because of a thigh injury, spoiled Fery's hopes of launching a revival by immediately breaking back twice in the third set before completing a 6-3 6-3 7-5 victory.

articles.title: Deadlines, acrimony and a record as Man City back Maresca for Fernandez deal
articles.summary: The summer's longest-running transfer saga ends with Manchester City paying a joint-British record fee to bring in midfielder Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea.
body: City have paid a joint-British record £125m deal for the Argentina international to break their club record transfer fee for the second time this summer following the £116m arrival of Elliot Anderson.

City had to overcome numerous obstacles to finalise a difficult deal during the 79-day transfer window, from being set deadlines to complete the deal and the backdrop of former Chelsea boss Maresca's acrimonious appointment as their manager.
But shelling out a joint-British record fee showcased City's perseverance to acquire their man and those upstairs at Etihad Stadium have shown unequivocal faith to both player and manager.

City have started the season with back-to-back Premier League wins and Fernandez's arrival means he becomes the first player in football history to move for more than £100m twice after going to Chelsea from Benfica for £107m in 2023.

articles.title: Dodgers get reinforcements; Shohei Ohtani's status still uncertain
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers entered September with a crowded roster, a few familiar faces returning and plenty of questions to sort through with the regular season winding down.
body: The Dodgers activated catcher Will Smith, Dalton Rushing and left-handed pitcher Justin Wrobleski from the injured list Tuesday while adding infielder Alex Freeland to the active roster.
To make room, the Dodgers optioned outfielder Alek Thomas and designated catcher Ben Rortvedt for assignment.
With less than a month remaining in the regular season, the Dodgers are beginning to get healthier, but manager Dave Roberts knows the reinforcements also come with some limitations.

Smith, 31, has been sidelined since June 6 with a neck injury. Before landing on the injured list, he appeared in 52 games and was hitting.249 with six home runs and 23 RBI. He made five rehab appearances with OKC, batting.250 with two doubles and a home run.

articles.title: Man Utd fail in attempt to sign Ait-Nouri from Man City
articles.summary: Manchester United approached Manchester City in the final hours of the transfer window in an attempt to sign Algeria defender Rayan Ait-Nouri on loan
body: Manchester United failed in a shock deadline day move to sign Manchester City full-back Rayan Ait-Nouri on loan and also missed out on Leicester City's teenage midfielder Louis Page.
United have been trying to address a perceived weakness in Michael Carrick's defence for the latter part of the transfer window.

Having opted against pursuing deals for Barcelona's Alejandro Balde and Racing Santander's Jorge Salinas, and the transfer deadline less than 12 hours away, United decided to check if a deal was possible for Algeria's Ait-Nouri.
United sources say they were not interested in a permanent deal for Ait-Nouri and were told the only acceptable outcome for City would be a loan with an obligation to buy, which they rejected.

articles.title: Jays Lose To Guardians
articles.summary: Blue Jays 1 Guardians 6. The Jays had all sorts of troubles with Guardians starter Gavin Williams. Well, really just one trouble. They couldn’t hit him. Williams went seven innings and allowed just two hits and a walk with thirteen strikeouts. Our one run was in the fourth.
body: Our one run was in the fourth. Kazuma Okamoto led off with a single. After Andrés Giménez struck out, Ernie Clement went to a full count and the Jays sent Okamoto (surprising me, Oka is not fast and the Jays were striking out a lot). Clement took ball four, but the Guardians threw to second anyway. The throw was well wide of second and Okamoto went to third on the play. After Myles Straw struck out (I really thought that he had to make contact or we weren’t going to score at all today) Williams threw a wild pitch to Brett Bateman, allowing Oka to score. Oka going first to home without the help of a hit wasn’t on my bingo card.
The Jays didn’t have any more luck against Guardian relievers, Hunter Gaddis and Matt Festa.
The bullpen day started off ok, for the Jays, but didn’t end well.
The Jays had three hits in total. Kirk, Guerrero, and Okamoto had one each.

articles.title: Balogun walks away from Everton deal - after move scuppered Camara to Chelsea
articles.summary: Everton's move for Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has fallen through after a change of heart from the player - after the deal scuppered Chelsea's chances of signing Lamine Camara.
body: Balogun arrived on Merseyside at lunchtime to complete the £40m Deadline Day transfer, but doubts then started to emerge about the deal being completed during the afternoon as the medical threw up an issue.

As a result of this issue, Monaco then proceeded with a move to sell midfielder Camara. But in another twist, Everton renegotiated the terms of the deal for Balogun - which forced a dramatic move from Monaco.
With a full agreement to sell Camara to Chelsea in place, Monaco withdrew from the deal as the 11pm transfer deadline passed, which left the Blues furious.
Chelsea also had the chance to withdraw from the £125m move to sell Enzo Fernandez to Man City, but chose not to out of good faith.

articles.title: Deal off! Monaco pull out of selling Fernandez replacement Camara to Chelsea
articles.summary: Monaco have pulled out of the deal to sell Lamine Camara to Chelsea - who feel the French club have acted in an extraordinary and deeply unprofessional way.
body: Camara was set to join Chelsea for £47m and was to sign a six-year deal pending a medical.
Just after the 11pm transfer deadline passed, news emerged that Monaco reneged on the agreement they had with Chelsea, and they had informed the Blues of their decision in writing.

The reason for Monaco pulling out was that they had successfully renegotiated the deal to sell Folarin Balogun to Everton, but the striker sensationally backed out of the move at the very last minute.

Monaco only wanted to sell one player, and once they thought they had a deal agreed to sell Balogun to Everton, they pulled out of the Camara-to-Chelsea deal despite a full written club-to-club agreement with the Blues.
